output.summary: The rise in admitted-patient ED length of stay is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours). It began in March, when hospitalist rounding moved to 09:30 with new admissions first. Medical-ward discharges slipped later, while surgical wards did not change. A pilot with a quasi-random huddle schedule cut boarding from 4.6 to 2.3 hours. Nurse staffing hours, vacancies, volume, acuity and bed capacity were flat, so understaffing, volume and capacity are contradicted. The ED front-end problems are likely downstream of boarding, though the May triage-provider cut is a rival explanation. The September cleaning-staff cut is unquantified. Extend the huddle. Do not pause it or defer case managers to fund travel nurses.
